# Menu reference

This page lists every entry of the menus of the ABBA window, in ABBA 0.24.1, in the order they appear. Each command shows its dialog and its parameters, with their default values. The user guide explains when and how to use them.

:::{note}
Most commands act on the **selected slices**. Select slices first (see [Select & display slices](../guide/select_display_slices.md)), then run the command.
:::

(menu-file)=
## File

(menu-file-save-state-view)=
### Save State (+View)

{menuselection}`File --> Save State (+View)`

Saves the current ABBA session (slices, positions, registrations, display settings and view) to an `.abba` state file.

(menu-file-load-state-view)=
### Load State (+View)

{menuselection}`File --> Load State (+View)`

Opens an `.abba` state file in the current session. Start from a fresh ABBA window: a state cannot be merged into a session that already contains slices.

(menu-edit)=
## Edit

(menu-edit-undo-ctrl-z)=
### Undo [Ctrl+Z]

{menuselection}`Edit --> Undo [Ctrl+Z]`

Undoes the last action (slice move, registration, key slice, rotation, flip...).

(menu-edit-redo-ctrl-shift-z)=
### Redo [Ctrl+Shift+Z]

{menuselection}`Edit --> Redo [Ctrl+Shift+Z]`

Redoes the last undone action.

### Configuration

#### Startup Message

(menu-edit-configuration-startup-message-reset-preferences)=
##### Reset Preferences

{menuselection}`Edit --> Configuration --> Startup Message --> Reset Preferences`

Shows the startup messages again, including the ones you chose not to display anymore.

#### Mouse Options

(menu-edit-configuration-mouse-options-show-atlas-position)=
##### Show Atlas Position

{menuselection}`Edit --> Configuration --> Mouse Options --> Show Atlas Position`

Displays, next to the mouse pointer, the atlas coordinates of the point under it.

(menu-edit-configuration-mouse-options-hide-atlas-position)=
##### Hide Atlas Position

{menuselection}`Edit --> Configuration --> Mouse Options --> Hide Atlas Position`

Hides the atlas coordinates next to the mouse pointer.

(menu-edit-configuration-mouse-options-show-slice-info)=
##### Show Slice Info

{menuselection}`Edit --> Configuration --> Mouse Options --> Show Slice Info`

Displays, next to the mouse pointer, information about the slice under it.

(menu-edit-configuration-mouse-options-hide-slice-info)=
##### Hide Slice Info

{menuselection}`Edit --> Configuration --> Mouse Options --> Hide Slice Info`

Hides the slice information next to the mouse pointer.

### (Experimental)

(menu-edit-experimental-raster-and-cache-deformation-field)=
#### Raster And Cache Deformation Field

{menuselection}`Edit --> (Experimental) --> Raster And Cache Deformation Field`

Speeds up the display of the selected slices by computing their deformation field on a grid and interpolating it. Only useful after spline registrations. Experimental.

![Raster And Cache Deformation Field dialog](/assets/dialogs/raster-slices-deformation.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Grid spacing (micrometers) | Spacing of the grid on which the deformation is computed. Larger is faster but less accurate. Must be above the atlas resolution. | `150` |

(menu-edit-experimental-raster-slice)=
#### Raster Slice

{menuselection}`Edit --> (Experimental) --> Raster Slice`

Speeds up the display of the selected slices by computing and caching their registered image at a fixed pixel size. The cached image has a lower resolution than the original image. Experimental.

![Raster Slice dialog](/assets/dialogs/raster-slices.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Pixel size (micrometers) | Pixel size of the cached images: larger is faster and uses less memory, but is blurrier. | `10` |
| Interpolate | If checked, pixels are linearly interpolated when resampled; otherwise the nearest pixel is used. | unchecked |

(menu-import)=
## Import

(menu-import-import-qupath-project)=
### Import QuPath Project

{menuselection}`Import --> Import QuPath Project`

Imports all images of a QuPath project as slices, one slice per project image, all channels included. Registrations can then be exported back to the QuPath project. Do not add or remove images in the QuPath project after the import.

![Import QuPath Project dialog](/assets/dialogs/import-slices-from-qupath.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| QuPath project file (.qpproj) | The project.qpproj file of the QuPath project to import. |  |
| Position of the first slice (mm) | Initial position of the first imported slice along the atlas slicing axis, in mm, as the Z shown in the slice information (0 = front of the atlas). Positions can be adjusted later, for instance with DeepSlice. | `0` |
| Spacing between slices (mm) | Distance between consecutive imported slices along the slicing axis, in mm. Use a negative value to reverse their order. Cannot be 0. | `0` |

(menu-import-import-current-imagej-window)=
### Import Current ImageJ Window

{menuselection}`Import --> Import Current ImageJ Window`

Imports an image opened in ImageJ as a single slice, all channels included. The image should be calibrated (pixel size).

![Import Current ImageJ Window dialog](/assets/dialogs/import-slice-from-imageplus.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Slice position (mm) | Initial position of the slice along the atlas slicing axis, in mm, as the Z shown in the slice information (0 = front of the atlas). | `0` |

(menu-import-import-with-bio-formats)=
### Import With Bio-Formats

{menuselection}`Import --> Import With Bio-Formats`

Imports images from Bio-Formats compatible files (vsi, czi, ome.tiff, lif...) as slices. Each image series of each file becomes one slice, all channels included. The imported slices are selected.

![Import With Bio-Formats dialog](/assets/dialogs/import-slices-from-files.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Dataset name | Name of the dataset grouping the imported images in the BigDataViewer-Playground source tree. |  |
| Files to import | Image files to open with Bio-Formats. Files should have a pixel size calibration. |  |
| Split RGB channels | If checked, RGB images are split into three channels (red, green, blue); otherwise they are kept as a single RGB channel. | unchecked |
| Position of the first slice (mm) | Initial position of the first imported slice along the atlas slicing axis, in mm, as the Z shown in the slice information (0 = front of the atlas). Positions can be adjusted later, for instance with DeepSlice. | `0` |
| Spacing between slices (mm) | Distance between consecutive imported slices along the slicing axis, in mm. Use a negative value to reverse their order. | `0` |

(menu-import-import-quicknii-project)=
### Import QuickNII Project

{menuselection}`Import --> Import QuickNII Project`

Imports the images of a QuickNII series (JSON file, also produced by DeepSlice) as slices, together with their registration: slice positions, in-plane affine transforms and atlas slicing angle. The import is approximate: a single slicing angle (median of all slices) is applied to all slices.

![Import QuickNII Project dialog](/assets/dialogs/import-slices-from-quicknii.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Split RGB channels | If checked, RGB images are split into three channels (red, green, blue); otherwise they are kept as a single RGB channel. | unchecked |
| QuickNII file (.json) | QuickNII series file, in JSON format. The images it references must be in the same folder. |  |

(menu-import-import-sources-from-bdv-playground)=
### Import Sources From BDV-Playground

{menuselection}`Import --> Import Sources From BDV-Playground`

Imports BigDataViewer-Playground sources as a single slice: each source becomes one channel of the slice.

![Import Sources From BDV-Playground dialog](/assets/dialogs/import-slice-from-sources.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Slice position (mm) | Initial position of the slice along the atlas slicing axis, in mm, as the Z shown in the slice information (0 = front of the atlas). | `0` |
| Sources (channels) | Sources forming the slice, one per channel, in channel order. Their calibration should be in mm. |  |

(menu-import-import-standardized-abba-project-zip-in-new-abba-instance)=
### Import Standardized ABBA Project (Zip) in new ABBA instance

{menuselection}`Import --> Import Standardized ABBA Project (Zip) in new ABBA instance`

Opens a standardized ABBA project zip, created with 'Export Standardized ABBA Project (Zip)', in a new ABBA window: the atlas and slicing orientation stored in the zip are loaded, then the downscaled slices and their registrations.

A file chooser opens to select the **Standardized project (.zip)**: Zip file created with 'Export Standardized ABBA Project (Zip)'.

(menu-import-open-demo-slices-from-omero)=
### Open Demo Slices From OMERO

{menuselection}`Import --> Open Demo Slices From OMERO`

Imports demo mouse brain sections streamed from a public OMERO server, through a QuPath project downloaded from Zenodo. Requires an internet connection and the OMERO dependencies.

![Open Demo Slices From OMERO dialog](/assets/dialogs/import-demo-slices-omero.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Demo dataset | '25 sections': a subset, faster to try ABBA. '97 sections': the full brain. Choices: `25 sections`, `97 sections`. |  |
| QuPath project folder (optional) | Existing folder where the demo QuPath project is downloaded, to keep it and export registrations to it. If empty or missing, a temporary folder is used. |  |

(menu-import-open-demo-slices-from-zenodo)=
### Open Demo Slices From ZENODO

{menuselection}`Import --> Open Demo Slices From ZENODO`

Imports demo mouse brain sections from whole slide images (vsi) downloaded from Zenodo and cached locally (about 1 GB per slide). The label and overview images of each slide are imported as extra slices (their name does not contain '10x'). All slices are selected at the end.

![Open Demo Slices From ZENODO dialog](/assets/dialogs/import-demo-slices-zenodo.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Number of slides | Number of slides to download, from 1 to 7, picked around the central slide. Each slide contains several sections. | `1` |

(menu-view)=
## View

### Display Mode

(menu-view-display-mode-positioning-mode)=
#### Positioning Mode

{menuselection}`View --> Display Mode --> Positioning Mode`

Switches to the positioning mode: all slices are displayed side by side along the atlas, to sort them and position them along the slicing axis.

(menu-view-display-mode-review-mode)=
#### Review Mode

{menuselection}`View --> Display Mode --> Review Mode`

Switches to the review mode: one slice at a time is overlaid on the atlas, to check and refine its registration.

(menu-view-display-mode-positioning-change-overlap-mode-o)=
#### Positioning - Change Overlap Mode [O]

{menuselection}`View --> Display Mode --> Positioning - Change Overlap Mode [O]`

In positioning mode, cycles through the ways slices are drawn relative to the atlas and to each other.

### Cards

(menu-view-cards-expand-card-panel)=
#### Expand Card Panel

{menuselection}`View --> Cards --> Expand Card Panel`

Opens the side panel that contains the cards (atlas display, slice display, editing tools...).

(menu-view-cards-collapse-card-panel)=
#### Collapse Card Panel

{menuselection}`View --> Cards --> Collapse Card Panel`

Closes the side panel.

(menu-view-cards-add-resources-monitor)=
#### Add Resources Monitor

{menuselection}`View --> Cards --> Add Resources Monitor`

Adds a card that monitors memory and CPU usage, useful when many registrations run in parallel.

### Navigate

(menu-view-navigate-next-slice-right)=
#### Next Slice [Right]

{menuselection}`View --> Navigate --> Next Slice [Right]`

Makes the next slice along the atlas the current slice.

(menu-view-navigate-previous-slice-left)=
#### Previous Slice [Left]

{menuselection}`View --> Navigate --> Previous Slice [Left]`

Makes the previous slice along the atlas the current slice.

(menu-view-navigate-center-on-current-slice-c)=
#### Center On Current Slice [C]

{menuselection}`View --> Navigate --> Center On Current Slice [C]`

Centers the view on the current slice.

(menu-view-navigate-center-on-atlas)=
#### Center On Atlas

{menuselection}`View --> Navigate --> Center On Atlas`

Centers the view on the atlas and zooms to fit the window.

(menu-view-log)=
### Log

{menuselection}`View --> Log`

Opens a debug window which logs the slice events of an ABBA session (creation, deletion, actions).

![Log dialog](/assets/dialogs/abba-start-log.png){.dialog}

(menu-slices)=
## Slices

(menu-slices-select-all-slices-ctrl-a)=
### Select All Slices [Ctrl+A]

{menuselection}`Slices --> Select All Slices [Ctrl+A]`

Selects all slices.

(menu-slices-deselect-all-slices-ctrl-shift-a)=
### Deselect All Slices [Ctrl+Shift+A]

{menuselection}`Slices --> Deselect All Slices [Ctrl+Shift+A]`

Deselects all slices.

(menu-slices-select-slices)=
### Select Slices

{menuselection}`Slices --> Select Slices`

Adds slices to the current selection, by index. Already selected slices stay selected. Most commands act on the selected slices.

![Select Slices dialog](/assets/dialogs/set-slices-selected.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Slice indices | 0-based indices of the slices, in the order along the slicing axis. '*' for all slices, comma separated values ('0,3'), inclusive ranges ('2:5'), ranges with a step ('0:2:10'). Negative indices count from the end: -1 is the last slice. | `*` |

(menu-slices-deselect-slices)=
### Deselect Slices

{menuselection}`Slices --> Deselect Slices`

Removes slices from the current selection, by index. Other slices keep their selection state.

![Deselect Slices dialog](/assets/dialogs/set-slices-deselected.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Slice indices | 0-based indices of the slices, in the order along the slicing axis. '*' for all slices, comma separated values ('0,3'), inclusive ranges ('2:5'), ranges with a step ('0:2:10'). Negative indices count from the end: -1 is the last slice. | `*` |

(menu-slices-remove-slices)=
### Remove Slices

{menuselection}`Slices --> Remove Slices`

Removes the selected slices from the session. This can be undone.

(menu-slices-re-index-slices-channels)=
### Re-Index Slices channels

{menuselection}`Slices --> Re-Index Slices channels`

Reorders, removes or duplicates the channels of the selected slices. Each selected slice is replaced by a new slice with the new channels, at the same position and with the same registrations. The same channel order is applied to all selected slices.

![Re-Index Slices channels dialog](/assets/dialogs/reindex-slices.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| New channel order | Comma separated 0-based indices of the original channels, in their new order: '0,2' keeps the first and third channels, '1,0' swaps the first two channels. |  |

(menu-slices-set-white-background)=
### Set White Background

{menuselection}`Slices --> Set White Background`

For brightfield images with a white background: the area outside of the selected slices images is filled with this value instead of black, which avoids dark edges during registrations and exports. Works for 8-bit, 16-bit and RGB images.

![Set White Background dialog](/assets/dialogs/set-slices-background.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Background value | Pixel value used outside of the images: 255 for 8-bit or RGB images, 65535 for 16-bit images. | `255` |

(menu-slices-set-slices-display-range)=
### Set Slices Display Range

{menuselection}`Slices --> Set Slices Display Range`

Sets the display range (min and max displayed values) of channels of the selected slices. Besides the display, it changes the images sent to DeepSlice: avoid saturated images.

![Set Slices Display Range dialog](/assets/dialogs/set-slices-display-range.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Channels | 0-based indices of the channels to adjust, comma separated (e.g. '0,2'), or '*' for all channels. Channels missing in a slice are skipped. | `*` |
| Display min | Pixel value displayed as black. | `0` |
| Display max | Pixel value displayed at full brightness; higher values are saturated. | `0` |

(menu-slices-distribute-slices-d)=
### Distribute Slices [D]

{menuselection}`Slices --> Distribute Slices [D]`

In positioning mode, spaces the selected slices evenly along the slicing axis. Key slices keep their position.

(menu-slices-mirror-slices)=
### Mirror Slices

{menuselection}`Slices --> Mirror Slices`

Turns hemi-sections into full sections, for instance before DeepSlice which needs full sections. The vertical midline of the atlas acts as a mirror: the half of each selected slice on the chosen side is kept, and its mirror image replaces the other half. Place the hemi-section against the atlas midline first. Undo with 'Un-Mirror Slices'.

![Mirror Slices dialog](/assets/dialogs/mirror-do.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Half to keep (as displayed) | Side of the atlas midline, as displayed on screen, where the tissue is. 'Left': the left half is kept and mirrored onto the right half. 'Right': the right half is kept and mirrored onto the left half. Choices: `Left`, `Right`. |  |

(menu-slices-un-mirror-slices)=
### Un-Mirror Slices

{menuselection}`Slices --> Un-Mirror Slices`

Removes the mirroring of the selected slices, made with 'Mirror Slices', while keeping the registrations done afterwards.

![Un-Mirror Slices dialog](/assets/dialogs/mirror-undo.png){.dialog}

(menu-register)=
## Register

### DeepSlice

(menu-register-deepslice-deepslice-registration)=
#### DeepSlice Registration

{menuselection}`Register --> DeepSlice --> DeepSlice Registration`

:::{note}
Only present when the session uses an atlas compatible with DeepSlice (adult mouse Allen CCFv3 or Waxholm rat), in coronal orientation.
:::

Runs DeepSlice (installed automatically in a local Python environment) on the selected slices: sets their position along the slicing axis, adds an in-plane affine registration and optionally adjusts the atlas slicing angle. The result depends on the slices display settings: avoid saturation.

![DeepSlice Registration dialog](/assets/dialogs/register-slices-deepslice-appose.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSlice model | Species DeepSlice was trained on: 'mouse' or 'rat'. It should match the atlas. Choices: `mouse`, `rat`. |  |
| Slice channels | 0-based indices of the slice channels sent to DeepSlice, comma separated (e.g. '0,2'), or '*' for all channels. Selected channels are merged into an RGB image with their current display settings (color and min/max). | `*` |
| Adjust atlas slicing angle | If checked, the atlas slicing angles (X and Y rotations) are set to the median angle found by DeepSlice. This changes the slicing for all slices, not only the selected ones. | checked |
| Pixel size sent to DeepSlice (micrometers) | Pixel size used to downsample the slices before sending them to DeepSlice. Defaults to 10.0 for mouse and 40.0 for rat; larger values are faster. |  |
| Ensemble (average of several models, slower) | If checked, DeepSlice averages the predictions of several models. Results may be better or not depending on the dataset: try both. | unchecked |
| Position post-processing | How the slice positions predicted by DeepSlice are corrected. 'Keep order': the current slice order is preserved. 'Keep order + ensure regular spacing': order preserved and slices evenly spaced, spacing estimated by DeepSlice. 'Keep order + set spacing (parameter below)': order preserved and slices evenly spaced with the spacing given below. 'No post-processing': raw DeepSlice positions, slices may be reordered. 'Keep current slice positions (in-plane registration only)': the slices are not moved, only registered in plane. Choices: `Keep order`, `Keep order + ensure regular spacing`, `Keep order + set spacing (parameter below)`, `No post-processing`, `Keep current slice positions (in-plane registration only)`. |  |
| Slice spacing (micrometers) | Distance between consecutive slices. Only used with 'Keep order + set spacing (parameter below)'. | `-1` |

### Affine

(menu-register-affine-rotate)=
#### Rotate

{menuselection}`Register --> Affine --> Rotate`

Rotates the selected slices around the center of the registration ROI. Z: in-plane rotation, clockwise on screen. X or Y: 180 or -180 degrees only (flip)

![Rotate dialog](/assets/dialogs/rotate-slices.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Rotation axis | 'Z': in-plane rotation, any angle. 'X' or 'Y': flips the section upside down or left-right, only 180 or -180 degrees are accepted. Choices: `Z`, `Y`, `X`. |  |
| Angle (degrees) | Rotation angle. Around Z, positive is clockwise on screen. | `0` |

(menu-register-affine-elastix-registration-affine)=
#### Elastix Registration (Affine)

{menuselection}`Register --> Affine --> Elastix Registration (Affine)`

Automatic in-plane affine registration (translation, rotation, scaling, shear) of the selected slices to the atlas with Elastix, restricted to the current region of interest. Atlas and slice channels are paired in order and must be equal in number.

![Elastix Registration (Affine) dialog](/assets/dialogs/register-slices-elastix-affine.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Atlas channels | 0-based indices of the atlas channels to use, comma separated (e.g. '0,1'). '*' is not accepted. The channels in index order are 'atlas_channels' in 'ABBA - Get State', and in the atlas display card. |  |
| Slice channels | 0-based indices of the slice channels to use, comma separated (e.g. '0,1'). '*' is not accepted. |  |
| Registration pixel size (micrometers) | Atlas and slices are resampled at this pixel size before being registered. Smaller is more precise but slower; 40 is a good start for a mouse brain. | `40` |
| Show registration images | If checked, the resampled atlas and slice images sent to Elastix are displayed as ImageJ images (for debugging). | unchecked |

(menu-register-affine-manual-affine-registration)=
#### Manual Affine Registration

{menuselection}`Register --> Affine --> Manual Affine Registration`

Manual in-plane affine registration: moves, rotates, scales and shears the selected slices with a gizmo, in a single dedicated window. Selected channels are only used for display. The result can be edited later.

![Manual Affine Registration dialog](/assets/dialogs/register-slices-manual-affine.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Atlas channels | 0-based indices of the atlas channels to use, comma separated (e.g. '0,1'). '*' is not accepted. The channels in index order are 'atlas_channels' in 'ABBA - Get State', and in the atlas display card. |  |
| Slice channels | 0-based indices of the slice channels to use, comma separated (e.g. '0,1'). '*' is not accepted. |  |

(menu-register-edit-last-registration)=
### Edit Last Registration

{menuselection}`Register --> Edit Last Registration`

Manually edits the last registration of each selected slice, if it is editable: spline registrations (Elastix spline, BigWarp) open in BigWarp, affine registrations (Elastix affine, manual, DeepSlice) open in the affine editor.

![Edit Last Registration dialog](/assets/dialogs/register-slices-edit-last.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Display the channels used by the registration | If checked, the editor displays the channels used when the registration was made, and the two channel fields below are ignored. | unchecked |
| Atlas channels displayed | 0-based indices of the atlas channels displayed in the editor, comma separated (e.g. '0,2'), or '*' for all channels. Ignored if the channels used by the registration are displayed. | `*` |
| Slice channels displayed | 0-based indices of the slice channels displayed in the editor, comma separated (e.g. '0,2'), or '*' for all channels. Ignored if the channels used by the registration are displayed. | `*` |

(menu-register-remove-last-registration)=
### Remove Last Registration

{menuselection}`Register --> Remove Last Registration`

Removes the last registration of each selected slice (it can be undone).

![Remove Last Registration dialog](/assets/dialogs/register-slices-remove-last.png){.dialog}

(menu-register-copy-registrations-from-model-and-apply-to-selected-slices)=
### Copy Registrations From Model And Apply To Selected Slices

{menuselection}`Register --> Copy Registrations From Model And Apply To Selected Slices`

Copies all registrations of a model slice and appends them, as they are (no new computation), to the registrations of each selected slice. The model slice itself is left unchanged.

![Copy Registrations From Model And Apply To Selected Slices dialog](/assets/dialogs/register-slices-copy-and-apply.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Model slice index | 0-based index of the slice whose registrations are copied, in the slice order along the slicing axis. | `0` |
| Skip the pre-transform | If checked, the model slice pre-transform is not copied: the out-of-plane part of X or Y flips, and rotations made with older ABBA versions. In-plane edits are registrations and are always copied. | unchecked |

### Spline

(menu-register-spline-bigwarp-registration)=
#### BigWarp Registration

{menuselection}`Register --> Spline --> BigWarp Registration`

Manual in-plane non-linear registration of the selected slices: each slice is opened in BigWarp, one after the other, where landmarks are placed by hand. Selected channels are only used for display.

![BigWarp Registration dialog](/assets/dialogs/register-slices-bigwarp.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Atlas channels | 0-based indices of the atlas channels to use, comma separated (e.g. '0,1'). '*' is not accepted. The channels in index order are 'atlas_channels' in 'ABBA - Get State', and in the atlas display card. |  |
| Slice channels | 0-based indices of the slice channels to use, comma separated (e.g. '0,1'). '*' is not accepted. |  |

(menu-register-spline-elastix-registration-spline)=
#### Elastix Registration (Spline)

{menuselection}`Register --> Spline --> Elastix Registration (Spline)`

Automatic in-plane non-linear (B-spline) registration of the selected slices to the atlas with Elastix, restricted to the current region of interest. Usually run after an affine registration. Atlas and slice channels are paired in order and must be equal in number. The result can be edited in BigWarp.

![Elastix Registration (Spline) dialog](/assets/dialogs/register-slices-elastix-spline.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Atlas channels | 0-based indices of the atlas channels to use, comma separated (e.g. '0,1'). '*' is not accepted. The channels in index order are 'atlas_channels' in 'ABBA - Get State', and in the atlas display card. |  |
| Slice channels | 0-based indices of the slice channels to use, comma separated (e.g. '0,1'). '*' is not accepted. |  |
| Number of control points along X | Size of the B-spline control point grid along X (minimum 2), the Y count follows the region of interest aspect ratio. More points allow more local deformations. | `10` |
| Registration pixel size (micrometers) | Atlas and slices are resampled at this pixel size before being registered. Smaller is more precise but slower; 20 is a good start for a mouse brain. | `20` |
| Show registration images | If checked, the resampled atlas and slice images sent to Elastix are displayed as ImageJ images (for debugging). | unchecked |

(menu-export)=
## Export

(menu-export-set-slices-thickness)=
### Set Slices Thickness

{menuselection}`Export --> Set Slices Thickness`

Sets the thickness of the selected slices along the slicing axis. It affects the 3D display (reconstructed brain) and the 3D resampled export, not the registrations.

![Set Slices Thickness dialog](/assets/dialogs/set-slices-thickness.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Slice thickness (micrometers) | Thickness of each selected slice, centered on its position. | `0` |

(menu-export-set-slices-thickness-fill-gaps)=
### Set Slices Thickness (fill gaps)

{menuselection}`Export --> Set Slices Thickness (fill gaps)`

Sets the thickness of each selected slice so that it extends halfway to its neighbors, leaving no gap between slices. It affects the 3D display (reconstructed brain) and the 3D resampled export, not the registrations.

![Set Slices Thickness (fill gaps) dialog](/assets/dialogs/set-slices-thickness-match-neighbors.png){.dialog}

### QuPath

(menu-export-qupath-export-registrations-to-qupath-project)=
#### Export Registrations To QuPath Project

{menuselection}`Export --> QuPath --> Export Registrations To QuPath Project`

For each selected slice imported from a QuPath project, saves its atlas regions and its registration (ABBA-RoiSet and ABBA-Transform files) in the QuPath project folder of the image. They are then imported in QuPath with the ABBA extension. Slices not imported from a QuPath project are not exported: slices opened from files can be exported with 'ABBA - Export Slices To New QuPath Project'.

![Export Registrations To QuPath Project dialog](/assets/dialogs/export-registration-to-qupath.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Overwrite previous export | If checked, a previous ABBA export of the same image is replaced; otherwise an error is reported for this image. | unchecked |

(menu-export-qupath-export-slices-to-new-qupath-project)=
#### Export Slices To New QuPath Project

{menuselection}`Export --> QuPath --> Export Slices To New QuPath Project`

Creates a QuPath project (QuPath 0.7) containing the images of the selected slices, with their atlas regions and their registration (ABBA-RoiSet and ABBA-Transform files), which are imported in QuPath with the ABBA extension. Only slices opened from a single series of a 2D file with Bio-Formats can be exported, one slice per image; use 'ABBA - Export Registrations To QuPath Project' for slices imported from a QuPath project.

A file chooser opens to select the **QuPath project folder**: Folder of the new QuPath project. It must be empty or not exist yet.

### ImageJ

(menu-export-imagej-export-regions-to-roi-manager)=
#### Export Regions To Roi Manager

{menuselection}`Export --> ImageJ --> Export Regions To Roi Manager`

Adds the atlas regions of each selected slice to the ImageJ ROI Manager, as ROIs in the pixel coordinates of the original (unregistered, full resolution) slice image.

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| ROI naming | Atlas ontology property used to name each region ROI, for instance its acronym, name or id. The available choices depend on the atlas. |  |

(menu-export-imagej-export-regions-to-file)=
#### Export Regions To File

{menuselection}`Export --> ImageJ --> Export Regions To File`

Saves the atlas regions of each selected slice as an ImageJ ROI set zip file, named after the slice, with ROIs in the pixel coordinates of the original (unregistered, full resolution) slice image.

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| ROI naming | Atlas ontology property used to name each region ROI, for instance its acronym, name or id. The available choices depend on the atlas. |  |
| Output folder | Folder where one '<slice name>.zip' ROI set is written per selected slice. |  |
| Overwrite existing files | If checked, existing ROI set files with the same name are replaced; otherwise these slices are skipped with a warning. |  |

(menu-export-imagej-export-registered-slices-to-imagej)=
#### Export Registered Slices To ImageJ

{menuselection}`Export --> ImageJ --> Export Registered Slices To ImageJ`

Exports the registered (deformed) selected slices as an ImageJ image, one plane per slice, resampled at the given pixel size within the current region of interest, optionally with the atlas regions as overlay. Same geometry as 'Export Atlas to ImageJ'.

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Pixel size (micrometers) | Pixel size of the exported image. | `20` |
| Slice channels | 0-based indices of the slice channels to export, comma separated (e.g. '0,2'), or '*' for all channels. | `*` |
| Add atlas regions overlay | If checked, the atlas regions of each slice are added as an overlay of ROIs. | checked |
| ROI naming | Atlas ontology property used to name each region ROI of the overlay, for instance its acronym, name or id. The available choices depend on the atlas. Ignored without overlay. |  |
| Image name | Title of the exported ImageJ image. | `Untitled` |
| Interpolate | If checked, pixels are linearly interpolated when resampled; otherwise the nearest pixel is used. |  |

(menu-export-imagej-export-original-slices-to-imagej)=
#### Export Original Slices To ImageJ

{menuselection}`Export --> ImageJ --> Export Original Slices To ImageJ`

Opens in ImageJ the original, unregistered image of each selected slice, at the chosen resolution level. Fails for images larger than 2 billion pixels (use a lower resolution level). Useful together with the regions exported to the ROI Manager.

![Export Original Slices To ImageJ dialog](/assets/dialogs/export-slices-original-data-to-imagej.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Slice channels | 0-based indices of the slice channels to export, comma separated (e.g. '0,2'), or '*' for all channels. | `*` |
| Resolution level | 0 = full resolution, 1 = first downscaled level, etc. Must exist in all selected slices. | `0` |
| Verbose | If checked, logs the progress of the image loading. | unchecked |

(menu-export-imagej-export-atlas-coordinates-of-original-slices-to-imagej)=
#### Export Atlas Coordinates Of Original Slices To ImageJ

{menuselection}`Export --> ImageJ --> Export Atlas Coordinates Of Original Slices To ImageJ`

For each selected slice, exports a 3-channel (x, y, z) 32-bit ImageJ image with the same pixels as the original unregistered slice image: each pixel holds its atlas coordinates, in mm. Waits for the registrations of the slices to be done.

![Export Atlas Coordinates Of Original Slices To ImageJ dialog](/assets/dialogs/export-deformation-field-to-imagej.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Resolution level | Resolution level of the original image the exported image matches: 0 = full resolution, 1 = first downscaled level, etc. Must exist in the slice files. | `0` |
| Additional downsampling factor | Integer factor to further downsample the exported image, on top of the resolution level. 1 = no downsampling. | `1` |
| Max iterations for transform inversion | Maximum number of iterations used to numerically invert non-linear (spline) registrations. Increase it if the inversion does not converge. Default 200. | `200` |

(menu-export-imagej-export-atlas-to-imagej)=
#### Export Atlas To ImageJ

{menuselection}`Export --> ImageJ --> Export Atlas To ImageJ`

Exports the atlas section at the position of each selected slice as an ImageJ image, one plane per slice, within the current region of interest. Same geometry as 'Export Registered Slices to ImageJ' with the same pixel size, so both images can be overlaid.

![Export Atlas To ImageJ dialog](/assets/dialogs/export-atlas-to-imagej.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Pixel size (micrometers) | Pixel size of the exported image. | `20` |
| Atlas channels | 0-based indices of the atlas channels to export, comma separated (e.g. '0,1'), or '*' for all channels. Depending on the atlas, channels include anatomical images, region borders, atlas coordinates, a left/right indicator and region labels. | `*` |
| Image name | Title of the exported ImageJ image. | `Atlas` |
| Interpolate | If checked, pixels are linearly interpolated when resampled; otherwise the nearest pixel is used (keep it unchecked for label channels). | unchecked |

### BigDataViewer

(menu-export-bigdataviewer-export-registered-slices-to-bdv-json-dataset)=
#### Export Registered Slices To BDV Json Dataset

{menuselection}`Export --> BigDataViewer --> Export Registered Slices To BDV Json Dataset`

Very experimental: saves the registered selected slices, placed in atlas coordinates, as a BigDataViewer-Playground json file which references the original images. Waits for all ABBA tasks to be done.

![Export Registered Slices To BDV Json Dataset dialog](/assets/dialogs/export-slices-to-bdv-json-dataset.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Output file (.json) | Json file to create. |  |
| Tag | Text stored as the 'ABBA' metadata of each exported source, to identify them later in scripts. |  |

(menu-export-bigdataviewer-export-resampled-slices-as-bdv-sources)=
#### Export Resampled Slices As BDV Sources

{menuselection}`Export --> BigDataViewer --> Export Resampled Slices As BDV Sources`

Experimental: fuses the registered selected slices into a 3D volume in atlas coordinates, resampled at the given voxel size and within the current region of interest, as multiresolution BigDataViewer sources (one per channel), computed lazily and cached.

![Export Resampled Slices As BDV Sources dialog](/assets/dialogs/export-resampled-slices-to-bdv-source.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Slice channels | 0-based indices of the slice channels to export, comma separated (e.g. '0,2'), or '*' for all channels. | `*` |
| Source name | Base name of the exported sources, '_ch<index>' is appended for each channel. | `Untitled` |
| Interpolate | If checked, pixels are linearly interpolated when resampled; otherwise the nearest pixel is used. | unchecked |
| Voxel size X (micrometers) | Size of the output voxels along the X axis of the sections. | `20` |
| Voxel size Y (micrometers) | Size of the output voxels along the Y axis of the sections. | `20` |
| Voxel size Z (micrometers) | Size of the output voxels along the slicing axis. | `20` |
| Z margin (micrometers) | Extra space added before the first and after the last selected slice along the slicing axis. | `0` |
| Downsampling between resolution levels X | Factor along X between two consecutive resolution levels of the output. | `2` |
| Downsampling between resolution levels Y | Factor along Y between two consecutive resolution levels of the output. | `2` |
| Downsampling between resolution levels Z | Factor along Z between two consecutive resolution levels of the output. | `1` |
| Cache block size X (pixels) | Size along X of the blocks computed and cached at once. | `64` |
| Cache block size Y (pixels) | Size along Y of the blocks computed and cached at once. | `64` |
| Cache block size Z (pixels) | Size along Z of the blocks computed and cached at once. | `4` |
| Number of threads | Number of threads used to compute the blocks. | `6` |
| Number of resolution levels | Number of resolution levels of the output sources, at least 1. | `6` |

(menu-export-bigdataviewer-export-registered-slices-to-bdv)=
#### Export Registered Slices To BDV

{menuselection}`Export --> BigDataViewer --> Export Registered Slices To BDV`

Shows the registered selected slices, placed in atlas coordinates, in a new BigDataViewer window. The sources are also added to the BigDataViewer-Playground source tree. Waits for all ABBA tasks to be done.

![Export Registered Slices To BDV dialog](/assets/dialogs/export-slices-to-bdv.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Tag | Text stored as the 'ABBA' metadata of each exported source, to identify them later in scripts. |  |

### QuickNII

(menu-export-quicknii-export-registered-slices-as-quick-nii-dataset)=
#### Export Registered Slices As Quick NII Dataset

{menuselection}`Export --> QuickNII --> Export Registered Slices As Quick NII Dataset`

Exports the selected slices as a QuickNII dataset: registered (deformed) slice images resampled within the current region of interest, and a series JSON file with the position of each image in the atlas. The exported images already include all registrations. The folder is created if needed.

![Export Registered Slices As Quick NII Dataset dialog](/assets/dialogs/export-slices-to-quicknii-dataset.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Output folder | Folder where the images ('<prefix>_s000.jpg'...) and the '<prefix>.json' series file are written. |  |
| Pixel size (micrometers) | Pixel size at which the registered slices are resampled. | `40` |
| Slice channels | 0-based indices of the slice channels to export, comma separated (e.g. '0,2'), or '*' for all channels. | `*` |
| File name prefix | Prefix of the exported image files and name of the JSON series file. | `Section` |
| Convert to 8-bit | If checked, images are converted to 8-bit before being saved. | checked |
| Save as JPEG | If checked, images are saved as JPEG, the format QuickNII reads; a single channel is recommended. Otherwise they are saved as TIFF. | checked |
| Interpolate | If checked, pixels are linearly interpolated when resampled; otherwise the nearest pixel is used. | unchecked |

(menu-export-export-standardized-abba-project-zip)=
### Export Standardized ABBA Project (Zip)

{menuselection}`Export --> Export Standardized ABBA Project (Zip)`

Creates a standardized, shareable zip of the current ABBA session: all slices downscaled to a given pixel size, their registrations, their deformation fields and metadata (atlas, slicing orientation, experiment information). The zip can be opened with 'Import Standardized ABBA Project (Zip)'. The session itself is not modified.

![Export Standardized ABBA Project (Zip) dialog](/assets/dialogs/export-std-zip-state.png){.dialog}

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Export identifier | Short name of the export, used in the zip file name: abba_export_<identifier>.zip. |  |
| Output folder | Folder where the zip is written. A zip with the same name must not exist. |  |
| Experiment information | Free text describing the experiment (animal, staining, sectioning...), stored in the metadata of the zip. |  |
| Slice channels | 0-based indices of the slice channels to export, comma separated (e.g. '0,2'), or '*' for all channels. | `*` |
| Pixel size of the exported slices (micrometers) | The original slice images are downscaled to this pixel size to keep the zip small. | `20` |
| Deformation field downscaling factor | The deformation field (atlas coordinates of each pixel) is computed every N pixels of the exported slices. | `4` |

(menu-help)=
## Help

(menu-help-check-for-updates)=
### Check For Updates

{menuselection}`Help --> Check For Updates`

Compares the installed ABBA version with the latest release on GitHub and shows the result in a dialog.

![Check For Updates dialog](/assets/dialogs/abba-check-for-update.png){.dialog}

(menu-help-ask-for-help-in-the-forum-web)=
### Ask For Help In The Forum (Web)

{menuselection}`Help --> Ask For Help In The Forum (Web)`

Opens a new post draft on the image.sc forum in a web browser, pre-filled with the versions of ABBA and its dependencies.

![Ask For Help In The Forum (Web) dialog](/assets/dialogs/abba-forum-help.png){.dialog}

(menu-help-go-to-documentation-web)=
### Go To Documentation (Web)

{menuselection}`Help --> Go To Documentation (Web)`

Opens the ABBA documentation website in a web browser.

![Go To Documentation (Web) dialog](/assets/dialogs/abba-documentation.png){.dialog}

(menu-help-give-your-feedback-web)=
### Give Your Feedback (Web)

{menuselection}`Help --> Give Your Feedback (Web)`

Opens the ABBA user feedback form in a web browser.

![Give Your Feedback (Web) dialog](/assets/dialogs/abba-user-feedback.png){.dialog}

(menu-help-about-deepslice-web)=
### About DeepSlice (Web)

{menuselection}`Help --> About DeepSlice (Web)`

Opens the DeepSlice guide website in a web browser.

![About DeepSlice (Web) dialog](/assets/dialogs/deepslice-documentation.png){.dialog}

(menu-cite)=
## Cite

(menu-cite-how-to-cite-abba-web)=
### How To Cite ABBA (Web)

{menuselection}`Cite --> How To Cite ABBA (Web)`

Shows how to cite ABBA and the tools it uses, in a window (requires an internet connection).

![How To Cite ABBA (Web) dialog](/assets/dialogs/abba-cite-info.png){.dialog}

(menu-cite-generate-methods-prompt)=
### Generate Methods Prompt

{menuselection}`Cite --> Generate Methods Prompt`

Generates a prompt describing how the selected slices were registered (atlas, slicing angles, positions, registration steps), to paste in a large language model to draft the methods section of a publication.

![Generate Methods Prompt dialog](/assets/dialogs/abba-generate-methods-prompt.png){.dialog}

(menu-cite-about-deepslice-web)=
### About DeepSlice (Web)

{menuselection}`Cite --> About DeepSlice (Web)`

Opens the DeepSlice guide website in a web browser.

![About DeepSlice (Web) dialog](/assets/dialogs/deepslice-documentation.png){.dialog}

(menu-cite-about-current-atlas-web)=
### About Current Atlas (Web)

{menuselection}`Cite --> About Current Atlas (Web)`

Opens the web page of the atlas used in this session, with its reference and how to cite it.
